title: The Red-Bud Tree
author: Ellen C. Babbitt
summary: 四位王子在不同季节看到同一棵树，各说各的样子。
publicDomainBasis: Retold by Ellen C. Babbitt and published in 1922 by The Century Co. (pre-1923, public domain in the United States); Project Gutenberg releases it as public domain.

paragraphs.en: Once upon a time four young princes heard a story about a certain wonderful tree, called the Red-Bud Tree. No one of them had ever seen a Red-Bud Tree, and each prince wished to be the first to see one. So the eldest prince asked the driver of the king's chariot to take him deep into the woods where this tree grew. It was still very early in the spring and the tree had no leaves, nor buds. It was black and bare like a dead tree. The prince could not understand why this was called a Red-Bud Tree, but he asked no questions.
paragraphs.zh: 从前，四位年轻的王子听说了一棵奇妙的树，名叫紫芽树。他们谁也没见过紫芽树，每位王子都希望自己第一个见到。于是大王子请国王的马车夫把他带到这棵树生长的密林深处。那时还是早春，树上没有叶子，也没有芽，黑黢黢、光秃秃的，像一棵死树。王子不明白它为什么叫紫芽树，但他什么也没问。

paragraphs.en: Later in the spring, the next son went with the driver of the king's chariot to see the Red-Bud Tree. At this time it was covered with red buds.
paragraphs.zh: 春天晚些时候，二王子跟着国王的马车夫去看紫芽树。这时树上已开满红色的芽。

paragraphs.en: The tree was all covered with green leaves when the third son went into the woods a little later to see it. He asked no questions about it, but he could see no reason for calling it the Red-Bud Tree.
paragraphs.zh: 又过了一阵，三王子到树林里去看时，树上已长满绿叶。他也没问什么，但看不出这树凭什么叫紫芽树。

paragraphs.en: Some time after this the youngest prince begged to be taken to see the Red-Bud Tree. By this time it was covered with little bean-pods.
paragraphs.zh: 此后又过了一些时候，最小的王子央求带他去看紫芽树。这时树上已结满小小的豆荚。

paragraphs.en: When he came back from the woods he ran into the garden where his brothers were playing, crying, "I have seen the Red-Bud Tree."
paragraphs.zh: 他从树林回来，跑进兄弟们正在玩耍的花园，喊道：“我看见紫芽树了！”

paragraphs.en: "So have I," said the eldest prince. "It did not look like much of a tree to me," said he; "it looked like a dead tree. It was black and bare."
paragraphs.zh: “我也见过，”大王子说，“在我看来，它不像什么好树，”他说，“它像一棵死树，黑黢黢、光秃秃的。”

paragraphs.en: "What makes you say that?" said the second son. "The tree has hundreds of beautiful red buds. This is why it is called the Red-Bud Tree."
paragraphs.zh: “你怎么这么说？”二王子说，“那树上有成百上千美丽的红色嫩芽。它就是因为这个才叫紫芽树的。”

paragraphs.en: The third prince said: "Red buds, did you say? Why do you say it has red buds? It is covered with green leaves."
paragraphs.zh: 三王子说：“红芽，你说红芽？你怎么说它有红芽？它满树都是绿叶。”

paragraphs.en: The prince who had seen the tree last laughed at his brothers, saying: "I have just seen that tree, and it is not like a dead tree. It has neither red buds nor green leaves on it. It is covered with little bean-pods."
paragraphs.zh: 最后见到树的那位王子笑他的兄弟们，说：“我刚看过那棵树，它不像死树。它既没有红芽，也没有绿叶。它满树都是小小的豆荚。”

paragraphs.en: The king heard them and waited until they stopped talking. Then he said: "My sons, you have all four seen the same tree, but each of you saw it at a different time of the year."
paragraphs.zh: 国王听见了，等他们说完，才开口道：“孩子们，你们四个看的是同一棵树，只是各人在一年中不同的时节看到的。”
